summary.text: Maritza Davila is the incumbent Democratic nominee for NY State Assembly District 53 and is unopposed on the November ballot. A longtime Bushwick and Williamsburg community organizer who worked with the Ridgewood Bushwick Senior Citizens Council, she has served in the Assembly since 2013 and chairs its Committee on Social Services. According to her official biography, she focuses on tenant rights, affordable housing and support for low- and middle-income families.

paragraphs.text: Born in Catano, Puerto Rico, and moved to Bushwick, Brooklyn, as a young girl, where she has lived since; raised three children as a single mother in Bushwick. Wikipedia gives her birth year as 1963.
Earned an associate's degree (AA) in Political Science from Long Island University in 2013.

Began her public-service career as a community organizer on education, healthcare, public safety, affordable housing, open space and economic-development issues in Bushwick and Williamsburg, and served on boards and advisory committees including community gardens, local NYPD precinct councils and area hospitals.

Served as president of the Community School District 32 board of education, and, while directing a statewide lead-paint awareness program, developed a concern for the educational needs of children with disabilities in Bushwick and Williamsburg.

Was a founding member of the North Brooklyn Coalition Against Domestic Violence, serving on its board for two years, and founded the Northern Brooklyn Residents Association, a community advocacy group that supported affordable housing and community development.

Joined the Ridgewood Bushwick Senior Citizens Council in 1996, where she helped found a local credit union, organized merchant, tenant and block associations, and worked on job training and affordable housing.

Won the District 53 Assembly seat in a 2013 special election, with 51.91% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and took office on November 6, 2013, succeeding Vito Lopez; she has been re-elected since.

In 2018 was appointed chair of the Assembly's Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force; as of January 2023 she is chair of the Committee on Social Services and remains a task force member. She also sits on the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Children and Families, Housing and Rules committees.

According to her official biography, she has worked on relief efforts after Hurricanes Maria and Fiona, COVID-19 vaccination access and food relief in her district, and hosts an annual Community Holiday Drive with North Brooklyn elected officials and merchants.
